newsitem.title: UK: British house prices rise 6.8 percent in year to February.
newsitem.headline: British house prices rise 6.8 percent in year to February.

text.p: British house prices rose 6.8 percent in the year to February, the Halifax Building Society said on Thursday.
Prices jumped a seasonally adjusted 0.5 percent on the month having fallen 0.7 percent in January.

"The latest figure confirms our view that last month's downturn was simply a one-off adjustment for the larger-than-expected monthly rises at the end of 1996," the Halifax, Britain's largest mortgage lender, said in a statement.
It forecasts annual house price inflation of seven percent in the fourth quarter of 1997.
The three-month on three-month rate of house price inflation -- 1.7 percent -- suggested the housing market continues to rise at a moderate pace, it said.
Prices paid by first-time buyers leapt by 2.1 percent in February, reversing January's two percent fall.
The annual rate of inflation for first-time buyers is now five percent, below the 5.7 percent rate seen the month before, but only because prices rose faster over the same period last year.
House prices are a key barometer of the health of Britain's economy since two-thirds of properties are owned, not rented. After years of stagnation, prices have now been rising for a year and more.
Last week, the Nationwide Building Society said British house prices rose 0.7 percent last month -- that put house prices 8.5 percent higher than a year previously, it said.
